chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from a man from our companions, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys plaster, so he measures some of it and takes the remainder without measuring. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Either he takes all of it based on his verification (estimation), or he measures all of it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying plaster by estimating some and taking the rest without measuring?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the validity of mixed estimation and measurement in trade, offering two permissible models to eliminate *gharar* (ambiguity): either accepting the estimation for the remainder or measuring the entire quantity. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precision in commercial contracts to prevent disputes arising from vague quantities. It reflects the broader principle that clarity in the subject matter of sale is a prerequisite for a valid transaction.
